about: Working rules every builder gets, whatever the pack. studio_pack.py adds them to a workspace's plan (conventions) and to the foreman's notes, so they are in every task prompt. Each rule says why: a rule with its reason gets applied to cases it does not name. Keep this short - it is paid for in every prompt. The foreman's own 'How to work' text already covers: read the test first, change only your files, never edit tests, run the tests before finishing.
all: Follow the brief's numbered steps and its algorithm as written. They were tried against every test before you got them; an approach you invent has been tried against nothing. If a step looks wrong or impossible, say which step and why instead of replacing it.

If no code could satisfy a check (the test calls a helper wrongly, contradicts itself, or needs a file you may not change), stop: name the test, the line and the reason in your reply. Working around it burns the attempt and hides the real fault from the planner.

When a check fails, find the cause before you edit: print the actual value and read the code that produced it. Never special-case the test's numbers or adjust a result afterwards to match; that passes one check and breaks the next.
After three edits that leave the same check failing, stop trying variations. Read the brief and the test again from the top: the misunderstanding is usually there, not in the last line you changed.
Make the smallest change that does the task. Do not rename, reformat or reorganize code the task did not ask about: older tests and later tasks depend on it as it is.

A loop over the data stays linear: inside it, no sum(), min(), max(), sorted(), list slicing, list copies or pop(0) on that same data. Keep a running total and an index. Real inputs here are hundreds of thousands of items, and one such call makes a second of work into minutes.

Import every submodule in the file that calls it (`import tkinter.filedialog`, `import os.path`, `import xml.etree.ElementTree`). `import package` alone does not provide `package.sub`; it only seems to when something else imported it first.
Run Python as `.venv\Scripts\python.exe`. The tests are plain scripts that print PASS and FAIL lines: run them as scripts, not with pytest.
When you run the program to look at what it does, send its output to the system temp folder (a full path under %TEMP%). A bare file name writes into the project folder and fails the attempt.

Work inside the project folder and leave the machine as it is: no installs, no PATH or settings changes, nothing copied into system folders. A refused shell command is an answer; do not look for another way to do the same thing.
Before you finish, read your own change (`git diff`): every changed line belongs to this task, and no debug prints, commented-out code or half-done experiment is left.

windows-app: A feature exists when a person can reach it: for each one, the event must be bound (command=..., .bind("<Double-1>", ...)) to the code. A method that nothing calls is not a feature.

Slow work (a scan, a pass over the whole result, a big layout) runs in a worker thread that never touches tkinter; it only sets plain attributes that the main thread reads in an after() loop, which also shows a count. Work on the window's thread freezes the window.

Never put a window, dialog or menu on the person's desktop while you work, and never call anything that waits for a person (mainloop, tk_popup, messagebox, filedialog): the build stalls until the time runs out. To look at a window, keep it off-screen: app.geometry("1200x800+-4000+-4000"), app.update() for half a second, then read winfo_width().

Tk details that pass tests and fail in use: keep every tk.PhotoImage in a list (an image without a reference shows blank); give the panes of a ttk.PanedWindow weights (without them a pane can start with no width); call mainloop() once, in the entry point.

Windows paths: "C:" alone is the current folder on C:, not the drive (use "C:\"); a file dialog answers with forward slashes; a folder junction is not a symlink to Python (test st_file_attributes & 0x400 before following a folder).
